title: Mushroom Wellington
subtitle: whole mushroom filling in golden puff pastry
excerpt: A vegetarian Wellington uses a layered filling of mushrooms, spinach, and walnuts wrapped in puff pastry. It makes a proper centrepiece for a winter dinner. Most of the work can be done ahead, with just the baking left for the day.
sourceNotes: The mushroom Wellington became popular in British vegetarian cooking in the 1980s and 1990s as a meat-free alternative to the classic beef Wellington.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble the Wellington up to 24 hours ahead and refrigerate unbaked. Glaze and bake from chilled.

content.text: The filling must be completely dry before it goes into the pastry. Any excess moisture will make the base soggy. Cook the mushrooms over high heat and squeeze out the spinach well.

items.prepNote: use 320g shop-bought puff pastry, rolled out

content.text: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over high heat. Add the fresh and rehydrated mushrooms. Cook without stirring for 4 minutes, then stir and cook for another 4 to 5 minutes until all moisture has evaporated. The pan should look dry.
Lower the heat. Add the onion, garlic, and thyme. Cook for 5 minutes until soft. Stir in the walnuts. Season generously. Spread onto a tray and cool completely.
Roll the puff pastry on a floured surface to a 30x40cm rectangle. Spread mustard down the centre third. Layer on the spinach, then the mushroom filling, packing it tightly.
Fold the pastry over the filling to enclose. Seal the edges with egg wash. Place seam-side down on a lined baking sheet. Chill for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 200C. Brush the Wellington all over with egg wash. Score the top lightly. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until deeply golden.
Rest for 10 minutes before cutting. Slice with a sharp serrated knife.

items.fix: Cook the mushrooms until completely dry and squeeze all water from the spinach.

items.symptom: Pastry is raw in the centre after baking time
items.cause: Filling was too thick or pastry too cold
items.fix: Bring to room temperature for 15 minutes before baking if very cold.

items.symptom: Wellington burst open in the oven
items.cause: Not chilled before baking or edges not sealed well
items.fix: Press edges firmly together and chill for at least 30 minutes before baking.

content.text: The Wellington format -- a filling wrapped in puff pastry and baked -- became associated with celebration cooking in Britain in the 20th century. The mushroom version emerged as vegetarian cooking grew in popularity. It now appears on Christmas and Sunday lunch menus across Britain as a centrepiece dish that competes with the meat original.
